notes: Goods vehicles, buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles over 3500 kg GVM, whatever the body. Comes before the light commercial rules, so a goods-registered ute or cab-chassis over 3500 kg is heavy. class_map.csv holds NZTA's own 3.5 tonne line: for goods vehicles (NA up to it, NB over it) and for omnibuses (MD1 and MD2 up to it, MD3 and over).

notes: Utes, by body, whatever type NZTA registers them under: a ute registered as a passenger vehicle is light commercial. No weight bound, so a passenger-registered ute over 3500 kg, and a ute with no recorded GVM, are light commercial by the body alone.
A goods vehicle's cab-chassis or flat-deck body. No weight bound here; the ones over 3500 kg were taken by rule 1.
Goods vans up to and including 3500 kg GVM. A van with no recorded GVM matches nothing here (rule 12). Vans registered as passenger vehicles are people movers and take rule 6 or 7.
Minibuses and light buses up to and including 3500 kg GVM, whatever the body. class_map.csv MD1 and MD2 are NZTA's omnibuses up to 3.5 tonnes.

Passenger vehicles whose canonical make and model model_segment.csv marks suv, at any confidence, with the vehicle year bounds that file states. A passenger-registered ute is light commercial (rule 2) before it can be an SUV. Passenger-registered vehicles over 3500 kg are not in rule 1's list and stay here.

Other passenger cars and vans, people movers and sports cars included: every passenger-registered vehicle of these bodies that model_segment.csv does not mark suv. A model it marks car or unresolved, and a model it has no row for, are passenger.
Motor caravans and special purpose vehicles up to and including 3500 kg: neither light commercial rule names them.
Motor caravans and special purpose vehicles with no recorded GVM (NZTA writes 0): neither the over 3500 kg line nor the up to 3500 kg line can be applied.
A goods vehicle of a body the light commercial rules do not name (trucks, articulated trucks, goods-rated station wagons) at 3500 kg or less. Over 3500 kg they are heavy (rule 1).
Three-wheelers (motor tricycles) that NZTA registers as passenger vehicles: not a car or van by body.
A goods vehicle or bus with no recorded GVM that no body rule above took (vans, minibuses, trucks): its mass is unknown, so neither the light nor the heavy line can be applied.
